content:
Former Fox News host Bill O’Reilly called out the White House for not having an official spokesperson to address the rampant tech outages in recent days, which have sparked concerns and conspiracy theories online.

“We may be under cyber attack here in this country,” O’Reilly said on his show Monday. “It’s possible. I’m not a conspiracy guy. You all know that. But we barely got this program on the air because Zoom is conked out or something, and uh, this is a string of technical meltdowns, and I don’t think, you know, four or five days in a row is a coincidence.”

Later in the segment, he continued, “So you got five in a row, and I’m not, again, a conspiracy guy. I’m not going to play that game. It’s a destructive game. Somethin’s goin’ on, and we don’t have a national spokesman.”

“We don’t know how anybody’s going to get out there and say, ‘Look, this is what we think it is. This is a coincidence.’ Coincidence? Five in a row?”

Multiple tech outages have been reported since Microsoft experienced major disruptions on Nov 12. Shortly after that, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stoppage, halting all air traffic for hours.

This week, customers with JPMorgan Chase reported problems accessing online accounts, triggering more disruptions. The banking company said the problem was not caused by a cyber attack.

“I mean, you don’t think we’re under a cyber attack of some kind?” O’Reilly asked viewers. “This is a coincidence? Five of these things? And the government, our government, is totally befuddled.”

The former Fox News host made a number of demands, including calling on Congress to develop a new department to “make sure we are not going to be attacked in cyberspace” and “pass onerous penalties for miscreants who misuse the technology” to harm the U.S.

“I’m a little teed off about this because this is dangerous, and I predicted every bit of it, every bit of it,” he said. “And when this AI kicks in, then we have lost all control because Congress has done nothing.”

He told viewers, “This is ultra serious for everybody.”
